title: Beeswax cleaning by solvent extraction of pesticides
author: Calatayud-Vernich, VanEngelsdorp, et al.

steps.title: Extract wax with hexane
steps.instruction: Dissolve the brood comb in hexane, filter the solution to remove solid impurities, then evaporate the hexane under a stream of air to recover pure beeswax (≈15–19 % of comb weight; e.g., 150 g comb yields ~23 g wax).

substeps.instruction: Evaporate hexane under an air stream

steps.title: Prepare 6 % wax‑hexane solution
steps.instruction: Weigh the recovered pure wax and dissolve it in hexane to make a 6 % (w/v) solution in a total volume of 250 mL.

steps.title: Extract pesticides with DMF
steps.instruction: In a 1 L separating funnel, combine the 250 mL wax‑hexane solution with 250 mL dimethylformamide (DMF), agitate vigorously, then let the mixture stand until two distinct layers form (hexane‑wax upper, DMF lower).

steps.title: Separate and repeat extraction
steps.instruction: Drain the lower DMF layer (containing extracted pesticides) and repeat the addition of fresh 250 mL DMF, agitation, and phase separation three more times for a total of four extractions.

substeps.instruction: Agitate and allow phases to separate
Repeat until four extractions are completed

steps.title: Evaporate hexane to recover wax
steps.instruction: Retain the upper hexane‑wax phase after the final extraction and evaporate the hexane under a stream of air (air steam) to obtain a semi‑solid, pesticide‑cleaned beeswax.

description: Beeswax samples obtained before, and after the solvent extractions were sent to the USDA-AMS National Science Laboratory in Gastonia NC for multi-pesticide residue analysis to evaluate the effectiveness of the cleaning method. Wax was analyzed for 199 pesticides and associated degradates as described in Mullin et al. [3]. As can be observed in Table 1, Table 2, Table 3, the solvent cleaning tested here is an effective method to decontaminate beeswax from pesticides. Pesticide incidence was reduced significantly in the three beeswax samples.
